kurz: Planning shows at a glance which milestone is active right now, how far along it is, who is working on what, and what is not assigned to any milestone yet.

schritte.titel: Read “Where do we stand right now?”
schritte.text: At the very top of Planning › Timeline you see the active milestone with its progress (“Final version 2.0: 3 of 8 tasks done · target 20.11.”), the next target and, under “Being worked on”, which agent is working on which task. A click on a task opens it.

Each milestone is a bar from its start to the forecast. The vertical line marked “Now” is now; hover over it to see date, time and what is running. Hover over a bar or a diamond to see title, status, progress, forecast and target date.

Completed milestones are hidden so that the active ones come first. “Show completed” in the overview brings them back, faded and with ✓. In the timeline below they are collapsed under “Completed milestones”.
At the very bottom of the timeline, “Without milestone (n)” lists every open task that belongs to no milestone. Assign one: `amw aufgabe aendern <no> --bogen <no>`.

werte: number of the milestone from Planning, e.g. 45 for B45
fehler: The lead creates a task while there is an active or planned milestone. The message lists them and suggests one. Assign with `--bogen <no>` or deliberately skip it with `--ohne-bogen`.
All milestones are planned or finished. Start the next one in Planning with “Activate”.
danach: “What the computer did today” below the overview is collapsed. A click opens it; it shows which runs ran on this PC today and which are waiting.
fragen: Why do I have to give a milestone when creating a task?

So that nothing disappears: a task without a milestone does not show up in the overview. Agents other than the lead may not set a milestone. Their tasks stay under “Without milestone” until the lead assigns them.
